description.purpose: A display as ONE cell that owns its own port: an HTTP + WebSocket listener, an object tree in its own cell.db, a component library that is data rather than code, and server-side rendering that is materialised -- a page load answers from memory and costs no cell call. It ships with the Vision token stylesheet, so a display looks like something before anybody has designed anything.
description.use_when: Wherever a colony needs a surface of its own: one instance per display, each with its own port. Instantiate it with add_nodes and give the instance the port it should own via override_params -- the template's 7800 is the first one, not the only one. Wire the event lane out of the cell if anything should listen to what a person does on the page; a display nobody listens to still works, its events just dead-letter visibly.
description.not_in_scope: No authentication and no TLS, ever (R-W8-2): put a reverse proxy in front of it, which is why the default bind is loopback. No routing of its own -- the pages table is the only route source, and there is no cell.surface key any more: it was removed together with the /surface/* path it declared, so a tree that still carries one is refused at boot rather than served by nothing. No application logic: it renders what somebody sent it and reports what a person did; what that means is the topology's business. And no design opinion beyond the token sheet -- components are rows, and a model may define its own at runtime.
examples: DIRECTIONS - in: object.create / object.update / object.move / object.delete / component.define / page.set / query as tool_call turns; two or more in one body are answered as one bundle with a results[] slot, the store convention. out: a semantic browser event as a source emission on hop.route 'event' (header carries event_name, session_id, page_route), and a tool_result reply per op. A browser event on a prop the component declared editable never appears out here -- it is absorbed as local CRUD plus a diff to every viewer.

THE PORT IS THE IDENTITY, AND A DISPLAY CAN STILL MOVE - a second display is a second instance with its own port, and the port is settled at instantiation. Since 1.1.0 (GH #410) port and bind are NOT immutable: a params update naming either rebinds the running listener, keeps the cell.db and drops the joined viewers, which reconnect. This retracts the earlier promise that such an update is refused as Immutable. Move a display with {"params": {"bind": "0.0.0.0"}}; an address the socket cannot take is refused as invalid_input and the old listener keeps serving.

WHAT SHIPS IN THE SEED - one page at '/', a stack root, a text child, and the Vision token stylesheet as an asset row at /vision.css. The seed loads once, on first spawn only, so a display that an operator has emptied stays empty across a wake.
